tools.name: npm outdated / npm view / npm ls
Node.js lockfile and node_modules inspection scripts

findings.title: Direct dev dependency pinned to a version the registry marks as deprecated
evidence: package-lock.json: packages["node_modules/eslint"].deprecated = "This version is no longer supported. Please see https://eslint.org/version-support for other options."
npm view eslint@9.39.5 deprecated returned the same message on 2026-11-22
npm view eslint dist-tags: maintenance = 9.39.5, latest = 10.15.0

Trail of Bits collector recorded signals.deprecated = assessed_clean for eslint; that criterion evaluates package-level deprecation and did not register the version-level message. The discrepancy is reported here from registry data.
findings.impact: Build-time only. No known advisory affects 9.39.5 today; future security fixes for the 9.x line are not guaranteed, so a later advisory may have no patch on this major.
findings.recommendation: Plan a move to eslint 10.x once eslint-config-next declares support for it. The move is a major-version change and requires a lint configuration check; no runtime code is affected.

findings.title: Type-definition packages published by a single human account
evidence: Trail of Bits collector: 'single human publisher (types) of 1 listed' for all three packages (raw/trailofbits-report.md, Findings > Build-time only)
Collector: no publish provenance for the three packages
npm audit signatures: registry signatures verified for all installed packages, including these
findings.impact: Build-time only. A compromise of the single publishing account would reach developer machines and CI on the next unpinned install. Type packages ship no runtime code into the built site.
findings.recommendation: Keep package-lock.json committed and install with `npm ci` so versions change only through reviewed lockfile diffs. No replacement is needed; DefinitelyTyped is the standard source for these types.

findings.title: Third-party design tooling executes a downloaded binary automatically on agent events
evidence: .claude/settings.local.json registers SessionStart, PostToolUse (Edit|Write) and Stop hooks that run .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable hook
Engine binary installed at %USERPROFILE%\.impeccable\bin\0.1.27\impeccable.exe with a .verified marker
impeccable is absent from skills-lock.json (installed by its own installer, not the skills CLI), so its version is not recorded in the repository
findings.impact: Outside the npm dependency tree and outside the shipped site. A compromised update of the tool would run with the developer's permissions on every edit in this project.
findings.recommendation: Keep settings.local.json out of version control, update the tool only deliberately (`npx impeccable check` before `update`), and disable the hooks with `/impeccable hooks off` if automatic execution is not wanted.

findings.title: No known vulnerabilities in direct or transitive dependencies
evidence: Trail of Bits collector (OSV): 0 advisories for 11/11 direct dependencies at lockfile versions; 0 advisories for 416 registry-verified transitive packages
npm audit: vulnerabilities info 0, low 0, moderate 0, high 0, critical 0 across 432 dependencies (prod 17, dev 378, optional 82)
findings.impact: None at the time of the scan. The result describes advisories published as of 2026-11-22.
findings.recommendation: Re-run the audit before each release and enable automated dependency alerts on the GitHub repository.

findings.title: Lockfile integrity: every entry resolves to the npm registry with sha512 hashes
evidence: package-lock.json lockfileVersion 3, 432 entries: 0 non-registry `resolved` URLs, 0 entries without `integrity`, 0 sha1 hashes
npm audit signatures: 358 packages have verified registry signatures; 88 packages have verified attestations

The remaining 74 lockfile entries are optional platform binaries for other operating systems (e.g. @next/swc-linux-*, @img/sharp-darwin-*) that are not installed on this Windows host and therefore were not signature-checked locally
No .npmrc in the project: the default registry is used
findings.impact: Tampering with a tarball after publication would fail the integrity check on install.
findings.recommendation: Run `npm audit signatures` in CI on Linux so the platform packages installed there are also verified.

findings.title: No install-time script execution in the tree
evidence: package-lock.json: 0 entries with hasInstallScript
Trail of Bits collector: install-time script execution assessed 11/11, flagged 0

node_modules scan: 0 packages declare preinstall, install or postinstall; 21 installed package copies declare only `prepare` (e.g. acorn, minimatch, lightningcss, keyv), which npm does not run for registry tarballs
findings.impact: `npm install` / `npm ci` does not execute package code at install time for the current tree.
findings.recommendation: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` is viable for this project and adds a guard against a future dependency that introduces an install script; `next build` does not rely on install scripts.

findings.title: No typosquatting candidates found in the resolved package names
evidence: Manual review of the 414 unique package names in package-lock.json: names and scopes match the expected dependency graphs of next, react, tailwindcss, eslint, typescript-eslint and sharp (@next, @img, @tailwindcss, @unrs, @emnapi, @eslint, @typescript-eslint, @nolyfill, @humanfs, @humanwhocodes)
Direct dependency names are spelled exactly as the upstream projects publish them; weekly downloads range from 3,058,665 (@tailwindcss/turbopack) to 668,203,298 (@types/node)
findings.impact: None identified. This check is judgment, not an automated measurement.
findings.recommendation: Review new package names in lockfile diffs before merging.

findings.title: Publish provenance and security policy absent for some direct dependencies
evidence: Trail of Bits collector: 6 of 11 publish with build provenance; without: @types/node, @types/react, @types/react-dom, eslint, typescript
Trail of Bits collector: 9 of 11 publish a security policy; without: @tailwindcss/turbopack, tailwindcss
findings.impact: Without provenance, a published tarball cannot be tied to a specific source commit and CI run. Informational; not a vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Upstream remediation only.

findings.title: Patch and major updates available; no advisory tied to the gap
evidence: npm outdated: react/react-dom 19.3.0 -> 19.3.1 (patch); tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/turbopack 4.3.3 -> 4.3.5 (patch); typescript 5.9.3 -> 7.0.2 (major); @types/node 20.19.43 -> 26.6.6 (major); eslint 9.39.5 -> 10.15.0 (major)
Local runtime is Node v26.13.1 while @types/node is pinned to the ^20 range
findings.impact: No security impact measured. @types/node 20 against a Node 26 runtime can hide API differences at type-check time.
findings.recommendation: Apply the react and tailwindcss patch releases in a routine update; align @types/node with the Node major used in production. No change was made during this audit.

findings.title: Next.js production dependency footprint is small
evidence: npm audit metadata: 17 production dependencies out of 432 total

Non-optional production packages: next, react, react-dom, scheduler, @next/env, @swc/helpers, tslib, styled-jsx, client-only, postcss, nanoid, picocolors, source-map-js, caniuse-lite, baseline-browser-mapping, detect-libc
next 16.4.6 published 2026-11-09 with a registry signature; collector: no advisories, repository active, publishes from CI with provenance
findings.impact: The code shipped to site visitors comes from a short, well-maintained list; most risk surface sits in build tooling.

findings.title: Repository-hygiene criteria not assessable in this run
evidence: Trail of Bits collector coverage: Dangerous CI workflow, CI token permissions, Checked-in binaries and Changes reviewed by a second person assessed 0/11 — 'the Scorecard API did not answer'
Publisher concentration assessed 5/11; 6 publish from CI with provenance, so the effective publisher set is not externally observable
gh was not authenticated (60 requests/hour limit); HTTP sources: 35 fetched, 11 errors
findings.impact: The absence of findings in these criteria is not a clean verdict; it is unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Run `gh auth login` and repeat the collector to fill the OpenSSF Scorecard criteria.

limitations: OpenSSF Scorecard criteria returned no data for any dependency (API did not answer).
gh was unauthenticated; GitHub repository signals were rate-limited.
Criteria other than advisories apply to the 11 direct dependencies only; transitive packages were checked for advisories, integrity, install scripts and names.
74 optional platform packages for other operating systems were not installed, so their registry signatures were not verified locally.
Dependency source code was not read or executed; the audit uses registry, advisory and repository metadata.
Typosquatting assessment is manual judgment over the resolved name list.
